tasks.short: Register people for programmes and notify them of acceptance.

steps.what: Collect applicant details and help complete the application form.
Check required fields, supporting documents and available places.
Decide admission and resolve eligibility, capacity or missing-document exceptions.
Copy accepted applicant details into the programme register.
Send acceptance details, joining instructions and any payment deadline.

tasks.design: Configure an accessible application form and programme register in the {WORKFLOW}, with criteria and joining instructions maintained in the {DOCS}. Required-field, document-presence and capacity checks prepare the coordinator's admission decision; approval changes the existing record to enrolled and triggers a template through the {EMAIL}. Keep assisted applications available at reception.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms, capacity lists and approval messages sit separately. Rekeying appears easier than agreeing one register and admission process.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, status rules and notifications can handle most steps. AI-assisted coding can shorten small integration work; no model is needed for the assumed checks.
tasks.still_hard: Document presence does not prove eligibility. Fair capacity allocation, unusual evidence and accessible assistance still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Explain requirements without discouraging applicants, recognise support needs and resolve admission exceptions fairly.

ambition.what: An applicant status service showing missing items and the next expected update.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time copying details and chasing updates, and more time helping applicants complete valid submissions. Admission rights remain with the programme coordinator.

reach.task: Resolve applicant questions about incomplete submissions.
reach.learn: Programme criteria, accessible explanations and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Review application delays and reception coverage.
reach.learn: Queue ageing, capacity constraints and staffing trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Configured self-service and record workflows are established capabilities; programme admission still needs its own rules.
Required-field checks, capacity rules and template notices can use deterministic workflows.
Solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects require assessment under GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: The programme is an ordinary customer or community programme, not statutory benefits, recruitment or credit.
Applications use defined fields and a finite document checklist.
Automated checks test completeness and capacity; a coordinator decides admission.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover one programme, existing platform configuration and a small pilot; they are not measured delivery results.
The access range includes privacy review and any employee consultation required by national rules; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Programme type, admission criteria and consequences of rejection.
Application volume, assisted-application demand and document formats.
Current register, available platform licences and access permissions.
Capacity allocation rules, retention periods and authorised approvers.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which checks establish completeness, and which require interpreting evidence?
Can the existing register support forms, approval states and notifications without custom code?
What happens when two approvals compete for the final place?
Which alternative channels do applicants need?
new_work: Maintain programme criteria, capacity limits and notice templates.
Handle incomplete applications and failed deliveries.
Review permissions, retention settings and admission logs.
Check that assisted applicants receive equivalent service.

tasks.short: Capture merchandise or material orders and route them to the department responsible for fulfilment.

steps.what: Receive the request and establish the requester, items, quantities and delivery needs.
Enter request details into a draft order in the {ERP}.

loop.input: Free-text order details or attached order document; structured requests bypass the model.
loop.output: Draft order fields with source references and unresolved item candidates.
loop.check: Validate schema, required fields, requester identity, units and item identifiers against master data; show uncertain fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per request; unresolved fields go to the receptionist without posting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured forms handle standard requests, but variable descriptions and documents need extraction. A bounded call is sufficient.

steps.what: Check item codes, quantities, availability, prices and delivery details.
Clarify ambiguous items, unavailable stock or unusual delivery needs with the requester.
Approve the order for fulfilment, including any agreed exceptions.
Send the released order to the responsible department and record the handoff.

tasks.design: Use a structured form in the {WORKFLOW} to create draft orders in the {ERP}; a bounded extraction loop prepares drafts from free text and documents for review. Configure master-data checks and an approval queue in the {ERP}, then route released orders to department queues with a recorded handoff. Receptionists handle clarification with the validation result already prepared.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requesters use inconsistent descriptions, and reception lacks a reliable bridge between incoming requests, item records and department routing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order validation and routing can handle the fixed rules. Bounded extraction handles variable documents, while AI-assisted coding can shorten integration work.
tasks.still_hard: Poor item data, ambiguous units, stock timing and substitution agreements remain difficult. Routing a request does not establish that fulfilment has accepted it.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the requester actually needs and negotiate practical alternatives when stock or delivery constraints conflict.

ambition.what: A reception order status service showing which department accepted the request and its next update.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time entering and forwarding orders and more time resolving unclear requests and stalled handoffs. Commercial exceptions and release authority remain with the fulfilment coordinator.

reach.learn: Order states, item alternatives and limits on delivery commitments.

reach.task: Triage failures between request intake and order creation.
reach.learn: Validation errors, access permissions and duplicate-safe retry procedures.

evidence.claim: Email and document order capture can check customer, stock and price rules, route exceptions and post into finance systems.
A vendor case reports 70% touchless orders at allnex; this does not establish a reception-specific saving.
Structured order imports and stock synchronisation are established capabilities.
Department routing, duplicate checks and release gates can use deterministic rules.

assumptions: These are customer orders handled at reception, rather than internal purchasing requisitions.
The {ERP} contains usable item, stock and price records.
Clarification is conditional; its share represents average time across all orders.
A fulfilment coordinator currently approves release, and that decision right is retained.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover one intake route and one {ERP} connection with existing interfaces.
Access work includes GDPR data handling and employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Whether orders are customer sales, internal material requests or a mixture.
Request volumes, channels, document formats and item ambiguity.
Available {ERP} interfaces, licences and approval features.
Who may approve substitutions, discounts and delivery commitments.
How departments acknowledge requests and report fulfilment progress.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: How much intake can move to structured fields without increasing requester effort?
Which validation and routing features already exist in the {ERP}?
Can every extracted item and unit be traced to the original request?
How will retries avoid duplicate orders and duplicate fulfilment requests?
Which failures require clarification before release?
new_work: Review extracted drafts and unresolved item matches.
Maintain item aliases, validation rules and department routing.
Handle failed transfers, duplicate warnings and unacknowledged handoffs.
Sample extraction quality after document or catalogue changes.
Maintain access permissions and order-data retention.

role.altitude: Reception shifts from repeated entry and forwarding toward assisted access, clarification and handoff recovery. Programme admission and order release remain with their designated coordinators.
reach: Customer service representative: resolve application and order-status inquiries.
Office administration supervisor: use queue delays to improve reception coverage.
Computer user support specialist: diagnose intake and transfer failures.
skills_to_grow: Accessible form assistance and clear explanations.
Checking extracted fields against source documents.
GDPR-aware handling of applicant and customer information.
role.ambitious_version: Reception becomes a service navigation point where applicants and requesters can get help completing a request, see its status and reach the person able to resolve a blockage.
